contract.words: Collect $6,000 of settled cash within 45 days using no up-front capital.

terms.proofCondition: $6,000 of cash settled into the owner's account within 45 days

strategy.title: No executable plan: the three signed cemetery surveys have no fulfiller
strategy.why: Three written acceptances at $2,400 ($7,200) would cover $6,000 inside 45 days (14 days to cash, $900 cost, $0 exposure), but the deliverable is an on-site GPS survey of every plot (30 human hours per survey) and the record names no fulfiller: fulfillmentOwner is empty and requiredCapabilities is empty, so Brain cannot perform it and nobody else is established. Without a fulfiller the agreements cannot be delivered or collected.

alternatives.title: Owner performs the surveys
alternatives.why: Not on the record: nothing says the owner can or will do 30 hours of on-site GPS survey per association, and an on-site survey is physical work the owner is not named for.

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is correct and the decisive gap is the right one. Three WRITTEN_ACCEPTANCE agreements at $2,400 ($7,200) establish price and conversion. Recomputed: $7,200 is at least $6,000, and 14 days to cash fits 45. But the deliverable is an on-site GPS survey of every plot (30 human hours each), and the card names no fulfillmentOwner and no requiredCapabilities, so nobody on the record can deliver it. Brain's FULFILMENT link is false ('nobody has established who would do the work'). Without delivery, 'paid on completion' agreements never pay. Treating the owner as the surveyor would rest on nothing in the record (ownerPhysicalWork UNSTATED, no statement that the owner can do GPS surveys), so the plan rightly does not assume it. decisiveLinks = FULFILMENT, and the resolution (record a provider with quote, capacity and pay-on-completion terms within $900 per job) is what would make it executable.
findings: Arithmetic: 3 x $2,400 = $7,200 against $6,000. Two surveys ($4,800) would not reach the target, so all three must be delivered.

Timing is tight: if surveys take about 30 days and cash arrives 14 days after completion, the last payment lands about day 44 of 45. Any provider found must finish within about 30 days, or the target slips out of the window.

The card's $900 direct cost per job has no fulfiller behind it. For a 30-human-hour on-site survey, $900 is about $30 an hour, which may be low for a GPS survey provider. A quote must establish the cost, and any quote above $2,400 minus margin must be checked against exposure $0 (paid from completion receipts).
